evidence: deepseek uses "Floyd-W" and gpt-oss uses subset DP with "full = (1 << t) - 1"; both are solving the terminal-Steiner connectivity problem
affordance_in_statement: You are free to route these signals through any of the other non-priority towers in the network if it helps reduce the overall energy footprint.
removal_suggestion: Require the activated links to form one simple path containing all priority outposts, in any order, while still allowing non-priority towers as internal path vertices. This preserves the sample outputs: the first sample has path 2-4-1-3 of cost 3, and the second has path 1-2-3 of cost 2.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Subset DP over the at-most-ten priority outposts, followed by graph shortest-path relaxation
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: signals can be relayed automatically through any sequence of active links

common_affordance: The required network only has to be connected, so it may be an arbitrarily branching Steiner tree with shared non-priority relay vertices.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It appears to use shortest-path distances between priority outposts followed by an MST-style combination, which cannot account for sharing a non-priority relay subtree among several outposts.

It explicitly computes all-pairs shortest paths among priority outposts and therefore treats terminal connections independently; that is not equivalent to the minimum Steiner tree when paths can share relay edges.

recommended_edit: Replace the connectivity objective with: "The activated links must form a single simple path containing every priority outpost, in any order; non-priority towers may be used only as internal vertices of that path."
